James / Maya —

Per our internal review, Redwood can accept the retention carveouts as an MPA addendum with the following binding commitments:

1) Archival path: Redwood will perform encrypted daily exports of Aurora customer data to an escrow provider chosen by Aurora. Export files are encrypted with a customer-provided CMK (customer-managed key).
2) Retention & proof: Escrow provider will maintain 7-year retention and provide quarterly attestation reports; Redwood will include archival pointer metadata in our audit logs.
3) Export SLA & chain-of-custody: Full-account export within 5 business days; export manifest and SHA256 checksums provided to Aurora within 24 hours of transfer; transfer logs retained for 3 years.
4) Cross-border: DPA appendix will enumerate subprocessors and region-specific processing locations (EU/US/APAC).
5) Costs: escrow service estimated at $12k/year (ballpark) for accounts under $5M annual spend; exact pricing in the MPA addendum.

Next steps:
- Kimberley to accept the DPA redline changes and produce a clean DPA with the archival addendum.
- Karthik to publish the signed bridge letter + SOC2 summary to the shared Drive.
- Tessa to update the MPA timeline and confirm pilot start date of 2026-10-18 conditional on final DPA sign-off.

If that alignment looks good to Aurora, we'll queue the final documents and route for signature.
